title: Singing men's songs and why she avoids other singers' songs
summary: She says the Shakespeare songs were sung by men and women could do them, and discusses not encroaching on others' material, with Martha Tilton.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: Well, just let me ask you something. Of course, most of these were designed originally to be performed by males.

I guess this leads to a more general question. How do you feel about vocalists of one particular gender singing material that's 'properly,' and I supposed I mean properly in quotation marks, belongs to a spokesperson of the opposite gender?

Well, I felt that these particular selections were done by what would be considered the jesters or the minstrel in the court. And although, you know, way back four hundred years ago, there probably weren't any female minstrels, but why not! You know, why not! In fact, who's to say that there might

not have been some females dressed in male attire.
How about modern songs. This is something special.

This is one of the problems that good ol' singers have. Most pop tunes are written for guys. MR. HUGHES: Really? MS. SULLIVAN: Yeah. And it's very difficult to find songs that girls sing, you know. It's not easy. The guys can be as personal as they want to be. Like, "I loved you so and so and so and so." Girls have to sing songs in which they're not included, you know. Or else, it's got to be a put-down, like my 'Every Time, Every Time I Fall In Love I Get A Shoving Around Every Doggone Time.' But anyway,-- aut actually, to be frank, most of the songs that I picked for myself, are songs that I think Frank Sinatra, you know, would do well.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
You don't think he'd do that?

No, I don't think he'd do; (inaudible), and I don't want to do it either, you know. After Billie, I don't think anybody should sing 'Lover Man.' That's another thing, too. A long time ago when we were all singers were all, you know, looking for that special song to sing, we shied away from singing what was another person's song. they were identified with. And especially -- well, in this particular case, getting back to the female and the male songs, it would be easier for me to sing a song and get by with repeating a song that a male singer sang, you know, if it was suitable, than another female. Because that would be stepping on somebody else's material. It may not seem like much, but it's a very important aspect of our profession.
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Yeah. You're saying that you've been afraid to encroach on other people's songs?
Have other people encroached upon you?
